standard_prerequisites: I-adic completions N^ of submodules and density of N in N^; factorization of continuous maps into complete modules
Formal Spaces, closed lemma for (1) iff (2); Algebra, quotient-complete lemma for (2) iff (3); Algebra, hathat-finitely-generated lemma for direct summands of complete modules
core_obligations: (1) iff (2) is the Formal Spaces closed-submodule lemma; (2) iff (3) is the Algebra quotient-completeness lemma

For I finitely generated and (1): the inclusion N -> M factors as N -> N^ -> M with N^ -> M continuous; N dense in N^ and N closed in M force N^ -> M to factor through N, giving N^ = N + C with N a direct summand
A direct summand of the I-adically complete module N^ (using I finitely generated) is itself I-adically complete
proof_roadmap: Cite the two equivalences and set up the finitely generated case
Factor N -> N^ -> M and use closedness to split N^ = N + C
Conclude N is a direct summand of a complete module, hence complete
